messages:
harper: Heads up, ran into duplicate side-effecting requests from the Java/Kotlin SDK sample when users rapidly cancel and restart actions (e.g., tap submit -> back out -> submit again). Seems tied to coroutine cancellation not cancelling the underlying OkHttp Call reliably.

harper: Flow: UI button launches a coroutine that calls Retrofit suspend API. If user cancels (navigate away) we cancel the coroutine and immediately start another request. Occasionally server sees two POSTs for the same logical action. Repro on Pixel 6 emulator and Android 12.

harper: Minimal pattern in the SDK: Retrofit service call is invoked directly from a ViewModelScope coroutine using suspend methods provided by Retrofit. No custom CallAdapter.

lee: Retrofit's suspend adapter should cancel the OkHttp Call when coroutine is cancelled, but only if the adapter uses a cancellable suspend wrapper (suspendCancellableCoroutine) and registers invokeOnCancellation to call.cancel(). Are we using an older adapter or a custom wrapper?

harper: We're on Retrofit 2.9 with the community suspend adapter. But we also wrap results in a helper that does `withTimeoutOrNull` and retries by re-launching the suspend call on timeout. Could that be racing?

toni: Ah, withTimeoutOrNull will cancel the coroutine and then your retry logic immediately starts a fresh suspend call. If the original OkHttp Call isn't cancelled (racing edge) it can still complete and the server gets both. The suspend adapter usually cancels, but some edgecases exist when call is already in its terminal state or when using custom Executors.

lee: Two concrete things to check: 1) ensure the suspend adapter is up-to-date (newer adapters use cancelation hooks robustly), 2) audit any retry wrappers that spawn a new suspend call when the previous one is still racy-cancelling. Also check that your code isn't holding a reference to the underlying Call and calling execute twice.

harper: Example problematic retry wrapper: 
```
suspend fun <T> retryOnce(block: suspend () -> T): T {
  val res = withTimeoutOrNull(3000) { block() }
  return res ?: block() // retry immediately on timeout
}
```
This will re-enter block() even if the first call is in-flight and hasn't been fully cancelled at network layer.

toni: Right — instead prefer single-flight retry that respects cancellation: 
```
suspend fun <T> safeRetry(block: suspend () -> T): T {
  return withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
    try { withTimeout(3000) { block() } }
    catch (e: TimeoutCancellationException) {
      // ensure previous call is cancelled at network layer before retry
      delay(50) // small backoff to let cancellation propagate
      block()
    }
  }
}
```
Note: delay hack is meh, better to let the adapter/call cancel synchronously.

lee: Better pattern is to move cancellation handling into the network layer by wrapping Retrofit calls with suspendCancellableCoroutine that registers invokeOnCancellation to call.cancel(), and then in retry code check for isActive or use a mutex to serialize retries. Example: 
```
suspend fun <R> Call.awaitResponse(): Response<R> = suspendCancellableCoroutine { cont ->
  cont.invokeOnCancellation { this.cancel() }
  enqueue(object: Callback<R> { ... })
}
```

harper: Another datapoint: we saw duplicates mainly when users rapidly navigated and then retried via a snackbar action. The second request was often started on the Main dispatcher while the first was still running on the IO threads. The adapter should handle cancellation across dispatchers but if a custom wrapper switches dispatchers, we could be losing the cancellation hook.

toni: Also check that your connectivity listener or debounce logic isn't re-issuing the same logical request via a separate pathway (e.g., one triggered by UI and another by network callback). We had a bug where a LiveData update and an explicit user tap both called the same API with different request ids.

harper: Good call — I audited the code: the snackbar retry path posts an event to a shared LiveData which sometimes emits after the coroutine cancel race, causing two codepaths to fire overlap. Fixing the event emission to be consumed-only removed a lot of duplicates.

lee: Summary of recommended actions: 1) Use suspendCancellableCoroutine with invokeOnCancellation -> call.cancel() if you wrap Retrofit calls, 2) avoid immediate blind retries on timeout; instead ensure previous call is fully cancelled or serialized, 3) prefer call.clone() for manual retries if you hold onto Call, 4) add integration tests that simulate rapid cancel/retry and assert single side-effect on server.

harper: I've implemented: fixed snackbar event consumption, added a small single-flight mutex around retry logic, and added integration test that rapidly cancels and retries using an emulator. Local repro rate dropped to 0/200. Will open PR with fixes and tests.

ci-bot: CI note: adding the cancel/retry integration test to the nightly emulator suite. It flaked on arm64 emulators previously; mark as flaky-tolerant initially.

sdk-bot: Created issue for SDK docs update: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/256 to document cancellable-call patterns and retry best-practices for Retrofit + coroutines.

harper: Thanks all — will push PR and link tests. If anyone wants to pair on robust suspend wrappers, ping me.
